text.p: Romania, forced to submit to an austerity programme to revamp its economy, will have negative growth in 1997, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said on Thursday.

"Economic growth will be negative," Ciorbea told a news conference broadcast live, alongside representatives of the World Bank and European Union. "The exact figure will be disclosed at subsequent news conferences."

Experts from the IMF and World Bank are holding talks with Romania's new centrist government on a package of reforms which will enable them to resume credits suspended last year to the Balkan country.
Romania experienced 6.9 percent growth in 1995, one of the highest rates among ex-communist states in eastern Europe. But most economists described the growth as unsound.
Final figures for last year are still unavailable, but a forecast by the leftist government thrown out of office in last November's elections put it at 4.8 percent.
Central Bank governor Mugur Isarescu told the news conference that there was scope for a resumption of growth of the economy in the second half of 1997.
"While the negative growth scenario may come true in the first half of 1997, there can be scope for healthy growth in the latter part of the year," he said.
He said inflation, which hit 56.9 percent year-on-year in December, might rise in the first half of the year but would subsequently slow down. REUTER
